sections.title: The Altar of Burnt Offering
observations: In this section, God provides detailed instructions for the construction of the altar of burnt offering, which was to be made of acacia wood and covered with bronze. This altar was central to the sacrificial system, symbolizing the need for atonement and the seriousness of sin.

The dimensions of the altar reflect its importance, being large enough to accommodate the sacrifices that would be offered. The use of bronze signifies judgment, as fire consumes the sacrifices, representing God's holiness and the cost of sin.

sections.title: The Courtyard of the Tabernacle
observations: The instructions for the courtyard highlight the separation between the holy and the common. The courtyard was enclosed by linen curtains, emphasizing purity and the need for holiness when approaching God.
The entrance to the courtyard was the only way to access the altar, symbolizing that there is only one way to approach God, which foreshadows the ultimate sacrifice of Christ.

sections.title: The Oil for the Lampstand
observations: God commands the Israelites to bring pure oil for the lampstand, which was to burn continually. This represents the need for spiritual illumination and the presence of God among His people.
The lampstand's light symbolizes God's guidance and the need for believers to be filled with the Holy Spirit, reflecting the light of Christ in a dark world.

importantVerses.commentary: The altar of burnt offering is a crucial element in the sacrificial system, emphasizing the need for atonement and the seriousness of sin.
The command to provide pure oil for the lampstand signifies the importance of spiritual illumination and the continual presence of God.

questions: What do the dimensions and materials of the altar signify about God's holiness and the seriousness of sin?
How does the courtyard's design reflect the concept of separation between the holy and the common?
In what ways does the command for pure oil for the lampstand relate to our spiritual lives today?
